design.contrastiveGradientDefinition: grad(F_scarcity) - grad(F_stable) at the same RUL-021 pre-shock centroid
design.performanceTarget: time-averaged population persistence divided by initial population over matched 120-step homogeneous no-mutation probes

primaryCriteria.contrastiveGradientIdentifiable: >= 3/4 of seeds have nonzero contrastive finite-difference gradient norm
primaryCriteria.scarcityContrastiveAlignmentExceedsNeutr: >= +0.10 median paired cosine advantage over neutral bottleneck motion
primaryCriteria.scarcityMedianContrastiveAlignmentPositi: >= 0.10 median cosine with the contrastive scarcity-minus-stable gradient
primaryCriteria.scarcityPositiveInMajority: >= 2/3 of seeds have positive scarcity/contrastive-gradient cosine

interpretationBoundary: RUL-023 is an engineered ALife contrastive-selection diagnostic, not evidence about natural biological evolution.
The contrastive gradient subtracts a stable-resource local performance landscape from the scarcity landscape at the same frozen pre-shock rule centroid.
The scarcity component is reused exactly from committed RUL-022 probes; only the matched stable-resource probes are new in RUL-023.
The performance target remains short-horizon population persistence in homogeneous no-mutation probe populations and is not a universal fitness function.

Positive selection-specific contrastive alignment would strengthen the interpretation that environmental scarcity shapes the direction of rulial motion; failure would challenge that interpretation without erasing the observed motion itself.
